claims.statement: dcode cost estimates are display-only: nothing in the CLI caps spend or gates execution on them, so an incorrect rate only produces an inaccurate number.

The graph owns the durable per-thread cumulative cost total in the schema-private CostState channel `_session_cost_usd`, which uses an additive reducer (operator.add) so each write contributes only the spend it priced without read-modify-writing the running total.

Each cost update rides a graph checkpoint so cost tracking works for local, headless, and remote execution without a client-side state update; the client is a pure reader that renders the streamed total and never maintains its own lifetime figure.

`_SessionCostRecorder` is a LangChain callback handler installed process-wide for every model request (via `_install_recorder`) that collects one record per completed request keyed by thread and does no pricing, so agent, subagent, offload/summarization, and Auto-classifier calls are all covered with no extra wiring.

The recorder only collects while CostTrackingMiddleware alone drains and prices records; the agent's own response is priced from state only when the recorder did not already charge that message ID, so a request is never counted twice.

CostTrackingMiddleware.after_model charges every model request completed since the previous checkpoint and after_agent drains requests (e.g. the ReliableRubric grading agent) that spent after the final model step; both hooks catch exceptions because each hook is its own graph node whose failure would fail the user's turn.

The pricing loop catches BaseException around drain-to-return so a cancelled turn (CancelledError) hands drained records back to the recorder to be re-priced on the next drain rather than silently losing real spend.

A nested (subagent) CostTrackingMiddleware zeroes its cost channel in before_agent, checkpoints local spend on a private channel, and transfers the completed delta through the `_session_cost_transfers` map (keyed by checkpoint scope with owner_scope and total) for the owning parent graph to checkpoint even when a sibling interrupts.

The durable writer emits the thread's absolute cumulative total on a `session_cost` custom-stream event carrying {type,total,thread_id,pricing_ok}; total is always the full lifetime figure (never a delta) so a client that misses an event converges, and the TUI textual_adapter consumes this event to drive the status bar.

prepare_operation_cost prices a server operation's recorded side-model calls without committing them, returning a PreparedOperationCost whose update must be persisted atomically with the operation state or rolled back; a zero-delta prepare still consumes its records and must roll back if abandoned.
estimate_cost is the only function that imports or calls genai-prices, and the import is lazy so the package and its bundled pricing data stay off the CLI startup path.

estimate_cost forwards LangChain's inclusive input_tokens plus cache, audio, and reasoning detail buckets so genai-prices subtracts each bucket from its container before applying rates; only buckets the matched model actually prices are broken out and tokens in unpriced buckets stay in the ordinary input/output total.

estimate_cost returns None (unpriceable) for usage that reports only a combined total_tokens with no input/output split, for providers in `_UNPRICEABLE_PROVIDERS` such as openai_codex, and for missing usage or model name.
Cache token counts that exceed the inclusive input total are clamped (with a warning) rather than dropping the whole request, because genai-prices' calc_price rejects a negative uncached input.

dcode maps LangChain provider names to genai-prices identifiers via `_PROVIDER_ALIASES` (e.g. bedrock->aws, xai->x-ai, google_genai->google) before any pricing lookup, so the id it searches on is the post-alias id.

On the first successful genai-prices import a single daemon-thread updater starts, fetching upstream data.json hourly and installing it via set_custom_snapshot; it is suppressed by DEEPAGENTS_CODE_PRICES_AUTO_UPDATE=0, [update].prices_auto_update=false, or DEEPAGENTS_CODE_OFFLINE, and a failed fetch leaves the previously installed snapshot in place.

A local override catalog is consulted only on a primary genai-prices miss: the user's ~/.deepagents/prices.json first, then the maintainer-curated bundled_prices.json; upstream always wins and on a conflicting (provider id, model id) pair the user file wins over the bundled one.

prices.json uses the genai-prices provider-array schema (a bare JSON array of providers with per-provider id/name/api_pattern and per-model id/match/prices), and rates are per million tokens (input_mtok, output_mtok, and optional cache/audio/reasoning buckets).

prices.json is read once on the first request that needs it, so edits take effect on the next dcode start rather than mid-session, and a malformed file never breaks a model turn or disables ordinary pricing (the bad source is dropped).
The override loader (_price_overrides/_build_price_overrides) never raises: any unhandled failure warns once and caches an empty catalog so _override_price can treat loading as infallible.

Every bundled_prices.json entry must carry a price_comments field linking a tracked upstream genai-prices PR/issue, enforced by test_every_bundled_override_entry_is_priced_and_links_upstream, and entries are removed once upstream covers the model.

SessionStats accumulates turn/session totals (request count, input/output tokens, cache read/write, cumulative USD, priced request count, wall time) plus a per_model breakdown keyed by (provider, model_name) and a per_kind breakdown by UsageKind.

classify_usage_kind labels a request assistant, subagent, offload, or auto by whether it is the main agent and by stream metadata (summarization->offload, auto_mode_classifier->auto), driving the /cost per-type breakdown.

record_message_usage counts one API call once regardless of chunking: a completed AIMessage is idempotent on replay while a later chunk revises the request already recorded (via retract_request against the exact RecordedRequest ledger entry), so per-model and per-kind breakdowns cannot drift from the totals.
finalize_recorded_requests closes every request in a stream-round ledger at each round boundary so replayed chunks on an HITL resume pass are not merged a second time and do not double tokens/cost.

The end-of-run usage table is rendered by print_usage_table and gated by usage_table_enabled, which resolves [ui].show_usage_stats / DEEPAGENTS_CODE_SHOW_USAGE_STATS through load_bool_display_preference (default on) once so the TUI teardown and headless run cannot disagree; it fails open on config errors but re-raises a BlockingError.

/cost reports the current thread's estimate and, when a model has no rates, distinguishes an omitted model from a genuinely free request by reporting how many recorded requests are included in the figure.

Threads use LangGraph checkpoint persistence backed by a single SQLite database at DEFAULT_STATE_DIR/sessions.db (get_db_path, cached, directory hardened via harden_state_dir); get_checkpointer yields an AsyncSqliteSaver over a module-owned connection and thread ids are time-ordered UUID7 strings.

ResumeState declares schema-private checkpointed channels the CLI reads back from state_values on resume to rehydrate a session without replaying or re-tokenizing history, and because they are versioned channel state, resuming a specific checkpoint yields values as of that checkpoint rather than a thread-level aggregate.

ResumeState splits its channels by write path: model-turn channels (_context_tokens, _model_spec/_model_params, _last_model_request_at/_last_cache_model_spec) are written inside the graph on successful turns, while goal/rubric channels are written either by the TUI via aupdate_state or by graph middleware/tools, and both paths behave identically on local and remote graphs.

_context_tokens (from the latest AIMessage usage) is written by ResumeStateMiddleware.after_model and powers /tokens and the status bar, and _model_spec lets `dcode -r` restore the model the resumed thread was actually using instead of the user's global default.
CostState extends ResumeState, so the cost channels (_session_cost_usd and _session_cost_transfers) are persisted and resumed on the same checkpoint path as the other resume state.

delete_thread removes a thread's checkpoints and writes rows, invalidates in-module caches, and makes a best-effort removal of the per-thread offloaded conversation-history archive; its return value reflects only whether checkpoint rows were removed.

list_threads maintains a covering index idx_dcode_threads_list so the thread-list GROUP BY becomes an index-only scan, avoiding a full-table scan that would drag every inline state blob through I/O; index creation is idempotent and non-fatal if it fails.

sessions.py carries aiosqlite robustness for clean shutdown: _patch_aiosqlite adds a missing is_alive() required by langgraph-checkpoint, _drain_aiosqlite_worker joins the worker thread after close, and _guard_sqlite_handle keeps the handle closable when the opening task is cancelled.
